mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT has risen in every week of the window (-58.7 to -55.3), and transit ridership is a leading proxy for discretionary trip-making; a continued transit climb mechanically pulls RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT weekly means rose monotonically from -58.7 at t-3w to -55.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is at or below the -61.2 mean of the last 28 days while TRANSIT continues to rise week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The joint pattern of WORKPLACES recovering (-46.0 to -41.4) and RESIDENTIAL falling (19.7 to 17.1) means workers are leaving home again; it is the interaction of these two series, not either alone, that restores weekday retail footfall over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 4.6 points while RESIDENTIAL fell 2.6 points across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last-28-day mean even though WORKPLACES keeps rising and RESIDENTIAL keeps falling together.

mechanism_narrative: Recovery is policy-driven and visible in WORKPLACES; if the weekly WORKPLACES gain falls below 0.5 points, the reopening impulse has stalled and retail footfall loses its engine, driving RETAIL_REC down over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: week-on-week change in WORKPLACES falls below +0.5 points in any week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES weekly increments were +2.3, +1.3, +1.0 points over the window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite WORKPLACES weekly gains dropping below +0.5 points.

mechanism_narrative: Under mid-summer outdoor substitution, PARKS above -85 combined with RETAIL_REC still below -55 routes leisure time and spending to outdoor venues instead of indoor retail, so RETAIL_REC is flat or lower over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS weekly mean above -85 while RETAIL_REC weekly mean is below -55
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved to -82.6 while RETAIL_REC remained at -58.0 at t-0w
regime_hint: summer outdoor-substitution regime with indoor capacity limits
failure_condition: Next-week RETAIL_REC exceeds the t-0w value of -58.0 while PARKS stays above -85.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL has fallen 2.6 points in three weeks, showing households spending progressively more time outside the home; each point of residential decline releases roughly a point of out-of-home discretionary demand, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL weekly means declined from 19.7 to 17.1 across t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed its last-14-day mean despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to decline.

mechanism_narrative: Policy relaxation is revealed by grocery normalization: GROCERY_PHARM improving from -31.0 to -25.3 shows one-stop grocery trips no longer absorb all shopping demand, releasing trip budget to general merchandise and raising RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose 5.7 points from -31.0 to -25.3 while RETAIL_REC rose 6.1 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the last-28-day mean while GROCERY_PHARM continues to improve.

mechanism_narrative: If RETAIL_REC posts two consecutive weekly gains of at least 1.5 points, habit formation has crossed into self-sustaining momentum, and the following week's RETAIL_REC is higher than the week before it.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly change of at least +1.5 points in two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly changes were +1.5, +2.6, +2.0 points over t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: After two consecutive RETAIL_REC gains of at least +1.5 points, the next weekly RETAIL_REC mean is lower than the prior week's.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS mobility gains outpace TRANSIT gains, the marginal trip is being reallocated to open-air destinations rather than to transit-served retail districts; the divergence between these two series predicts lower RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: weekly change in PARKS exceeds weekly change in TRANSIT by at least 1.0 point
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS gained 4.0 points versus TRANSIT's 3.4 points across t-3w to t-0w
regime_hint: outdoor-favoring summer regime with residual transit aversion
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days exceeds its last-14-day mean in weeks where the PARKS gain exceeds the TRANSIT gain by at least 1.0 point.
